PFD-0001[3] confirms the physical discharge chain per reclaim stream — T11 → T11S separator → T12 (belt scale T12W) → hopper M16A-A-R01 with air blasters → clamshell + rod gates M16A-A-H01…H04 / M16A-B-H01…H04 → outbound belt T13 at 1,500 t/h — and that equipment is modelled as the CONFIRMED links L-H-A / L-H-B. It does NOT state that the H gates themselves select PAP versus drying, nor where the PAP and drying routes converge. The destination choice is therefore a separate downstream logical route/diverter abstraction (L-RTE-{A,B}-{PAP,DRY}, evidence DERIVED). Confirmed belt RATINGS (PAP six parallel 1,500 t/h conveyors, 3 running + 3 future; drying two parallel 1,299 t/h conveyors, both OUT OF SCOPE — PRO-0001 §2.1) do not make the ASSIGNMENT confirmed. Mutual exclusion per bank (one destination per bucket) is DERIVED from the single outbound T13 belt. The documented 10-minute gate/route changeover LOSS is NOT MODELLED: group switches are counted and penalised, but changeover_min = 0 on every link and no switching capacity loss is enforced.
assumptions.source: Q80130-MZI-M16-ME-PFD-0001[3] Rev 3, IFU, 28-Oct-2025 — Phosphate Storage Area flow sheet (equipment) + Q80130-MZI-M16-PR-PRO-0001 Rev 2, 22-May-2025, §2.1 (conveyor counts/ratings); destination assignment and confluence not stated in either
assumptions.placeholder: HUB:M16-RCL-{A,B} → L-H-{A,B} (CONFIRMED) → HUB:M16-T13-{A,B} → L-RTE-{A,B}-{PAP,PAP2,DRY} (DERIVED) + one conflict group per bank
assumptions.impact: which destination each stream may feed per bucket, the simultaneous PAP+drying mix, and any switching cost (currently none)
assumptions.action: downstream PFD sheets / GA giving the gate→conveyor→destination assignment, the confluence point and the real changeover behaviour

assumptions.text: M16 hangar numbering inside the bays is INFERRED. USER-DIRECTED / INFERRED: PFD-0001[3] shows eight 125,000 t hangars in four two-hangar bays but does not name them. HP-01…08 is the application's working convention (bay 1 = HP-01/HP-05, bay 2 = HP-02/HP-06, bay 3 = HP-03/HP-07, bay 4 = HP-04/HP-08), pending the plot plan and the official SMS pile-ID mapping. The bay topology itself (four two-hangar bays with the machine lines M16A-A-T06 · M16A-A-T11 · M16A-B-T06 · M16A-B-T11 · M16A-C-T06 interleaved between them) is CONFIRMED by the PFD, and machine reach follows the project-team bay-adjacency rule: ST01-A→bay 1; RC01-A→bays 1-2; ST01-B→bays 2-3; RC01-B→bays 3-4; ST01-C→bay 4. With Future expansion the same rule extends ST01-C to bays 4-5 and adds M16A-C-RC01 (bays 5-6) and M16A-D-ST01 (bay 6); the future hangar identifiers HP-09*…HP-12* are INFERRED display-only labels and are never solver spaces.
assumptions.source: Q80130-MZI-M16-ME-PFD-0001[3] Rev 3, IFU, 28-Oct-2025 — Phosphate Storage Area flow sheet + project-team reach rule 25-Jul-2026
assumptions.impact: which machine may stack/reclaim which hangar — solver candidates, ASP work-area validation and the mimic
assumptions.action: plot plan + official SMS pile-ID register to confirm the hangar names per bay

assumptions.text: CURRENT M16 reception is ONE shared 2,600 t/h envelope, not 2 × 2,600 t/h. CURRENT reception is a single 2,600 t/h path (M16A-A-T01 → T02 → T03/T04 → the three stacker lines): PRO-0001 §2.1.1 puts auto sampler M16VP01 on M16A-A-T01 and M16VP02 on 'the adjacent future conveyor', and PFD-0001[3] marks that adjacent line FUTURE. C1 and C2 therefore share one reception envelope — aggregate current reception is capped at 2,600 t/h, never 2 × 2,600 t/h. Modelled as a shared-capacity group on every stacking leg, so total stacking at M16 cannot exceed 2,600 t/h in a bucket whichever corridor the material came from. CONSEQUENCE: the S3 initial in-transit profile shows the corridors running alternately (C1 arrivals in the buckets C2 leaves free) instead of both at full rate in the same bucket — the alternation is DERIVED from this envelope, not observed dispatch history. A structural cap on simultaneous corridor dispatch, plus any reception buffer/interlock, still needs route evidence.
assumptions.source: Q80130-MZI-M16-PR-PRO-0001 Rev 2, 22-May-2025, §2.1.1 (auto sampler M16VP02 on the adjacent FUTURE conveyor) + Q80130-MZI-M16-ME-PFD-0001[3] Rev 3, IFU, 28-Oct-2025 — Phosphate Storage Area flow sheet (FUTURE marking)
assumptions.impact: maximum stacking/reception rate, corridor scheduling and the initial in-transit mass
assumptions.action: confirm the second reception line's phase, and obtain the reception buffer/interlock rules

assumptions.text: PAP-2 is a project-team requested second receiving-line planning option with the same 1,500 t/h / G10 demand and quality template as PAP-1. It defaults to FUTURE: its two route legs remain in the network with lifecycle FUTURE and availability false, while the configured 36,000 t/24 h demand template is retained but excluded from active planning demand. Selecting AVAILABLE activates both route legs without inventing additional M16 reclaim-bank capacity. PAP-1 + PAP-2 + DRY-FEED at their full templates request 91,200 t against the current 72,000 t/day two-bank envelope, so simultaneous full service is not claimed.
assumptions.impact: optional second PAP demand and outbound-bank allocation
assumptions.action: confirm PAP-2 physical tag, commissioning phase, downstream route and the capacity configuration used when it is available

CAMPAIGN_POLICY.basis: ASSUMED demonstration campaign/parcel policy — NOT a plant-approved operating limit. min_parcel_t 250 t is roughly six minutes of a 2,100-2,500 t/h yard machine and is chosen only to be clearly larger than the integer 1 t activity floor that produced one-minute stacking runs; min_run_min 20 min and max_hold_min 30 min are round operating figures of the same order as the documented 30-minute washing-line residence time. Replace all four with dated values from the equipment datasheets and the operating philosophy: minimum stable belt/drive loading, permitted start frequency per hour, drive-thermal restart limits, and the maximum period the plant accepts running an empty belt rather than stopping it. min_dwell_buckets is 1 (disabled) because no approved campaign-length rule exists yet.
